court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: 2nd J.M.F.C., Beed, case number RCC No.109 of 2020
case_name: Deepak Rambhau @ Rambhau Tate And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another

parties.respondent_defendant: Respondent no.2 (wife) and the State of Maharashtra

facts_of_case: Parties have arrived at aicable settlement; parties have jointly filed HMP No.F-41 of 2020 before the Family Court, Beed for a decree of divorce by mutual consent as provided under section 13(b) of the Hindu Marriage Act and granted a decree of divorce on mutual consent.

legal_principles.principle: The power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
legal_principles.held: The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303

legal_principles.principle: The High Court's inherent power to quash a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint has to be exercised in accord with the guidelines engrafted in such power, viz., (i) to secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.
legal_principles.held: In what cases power to quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or FIR may be exercised where the offender and victim have settled their dispute would depend on the facts and circumstances of each case and no category can be prescribed.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303

legal_principles.principle: Heinous and serious offences, such as murder, rape, dacoity, etc., cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled their dispute.
legal_principles.held: Such offences are not private in nature and have serious impact on society.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303

outcome.final_order: Quashing of FIR bearing criie no.18 of 2020 registered with Peth Beed Police Station, District Beed for the offence punishable under sections 498-A, 323, 504, 34 of the IPC and also the criminal proceedings vide RCC No.109 of 2020 pending before the 2nd J.M.F.C., Beed.

use_for_drafting: seeking amicable settlement in criminal proceedings
